state: We are correcting the CanMaintain contract for manager-driven plan edits and asset retirement. Both operations must work for 99/100/101/1000 independent records without making a large fanout one transaction. The source currently rejects edits with more than 100 matching future pending inspections and rejects retirement above 100 plans or inspections; an active-Plan invariant also continuously ties stored data to an assignee's current team role/work eligibility and the asset not being retired. Preserve original scheduled occurrence, frozen questions, inspector and finished inspection evidence. A change retains today's/overdue work as judged on its own date, while invalidating future pending instances and recording the initiating person/time. Current authority is required for admission, future generation, reminder dispatch and completion; historical truth must survive staff revocation. Delayed/repeated cleanup must remain correct across subsequent edits and asset reinstatement: old invalidation cannot be forgotten or applied to a later fresh generation. Existing records, immutable child facts, pure guards/derives, local CRUD hooks, committed record-identity notifications, keyed scheduling, next-ID continuation events and authorized record-specific recovery are available. They offer no generic app-visible queue/audit-history interface that can be assumed. Maintain must not own or optimistically release Rent's resource downtime/booking-review records. Keep ordinary finite local work limits, but do not change the workflow requirements to cap total plan volume. No new runtime/scheduler, blanket cross-service transaction or duplicate booking state may be introduced. This remains authored draft semantics with handwritten desired targets; prototype compatibility is not an outcome criterion.

progress.instructions: Select the minimal adequate design under the fixed requirements and available primitives. Evaluate the alternatives on equal evidence, count their real tradeoffs, and identify any uncertain prerequisite.

criteria.atomic_caps: Preserve all existing atomic loops and the active-assignee/retired-parent invariant. Larger requests reject instead of proceeding, so users must work under the current transaction count limits. The benefit is the present all-at-once cleanup with minimal schema; the price is noncompliance with the larger-volume workflow and dependence of historical configuration truth on changing current authority.
criteria.event_only: Replace bulk loops with small hooks plus continuation events containing fixed change date, template/retirement generation and initiating identity. Apply live authority checks when admitting effects. Do not store separate business cancellation facts. This is economical in model declarations, but a future use guard based only on newest plan/asset state cannot remember an earlier supersession after another edit/reinstatement; record-addressed inspection/restart also has no durable input absent an invented history/queue service.
criteria.owned_evidence: Author one contained immutable cancellation-intent record for each manager change, preserving old template revision or retirement generation, cutoff, person/time and reason, with owned cursor/result fields. Add an asset generation frozen onto each Inspection and advanced on retirement. Continue cleanup one pending matching inspection at a time, check retained boundaries at current inspection/work admission, and leave completed intents as cancellation history. Recovery is a guarded operation taking that same retained record. More local schema and queries buy truthful progress/evidence, stable attribution and correct old/new-generation behavior through retries and reinstatement, while leaving paid booking and room blocks with Rent.
